37: func (s *Server) setupGRPCInterfaces(config *Config, deps Deps) error {
38: 	// A server has 5 different gRPC interfaces
39: 	//
40: 	// * External - This is the main public gRPC network listener. This
41: 	//      is an actual *grpc.Server that we have listening on both the
42: 	//      grpc and grpc_tls ports. Generally this interface will not be
43: 	//      used by the server itself. All services which are intended
44: 	//      to be public APIs must be registered to this interface. This
45: 	//      interface is created outside of the server in the agent code
46: 	//      and then passed to the NewServer constructor. Some services
47: 	//      like xDS and DNS get registered outside of the server code.
48: 	//
49: 	// * Internal / Multiplexed - Our internal_rpc port uses yamux and
50: 	//      various byte prefixes to multiplex different protocols over
51: 	//      the single connection. One of the multiplexed protocols is
52: 	//      gRPC. gRPC in this fashion works using a custom net.Listener
53: 	//      implementation that receives net.Conns to be handled through
54: 	//      a channel. When a new yamux session is opened which produces
55: 	//      a yamux conn (which implements the net.Conn interface), the
56: 	//      connection is then sent to the custom listener. Then the
57: 	//      standard grpc.Server.Serve method can accept the conn from
58: 	//      the listener and operate on it like any other standard conn.
59: 	//      Historically, the external gRPC interface was optional and
60: 	//      so all services which needed leader or DC forwarding had to
61: 	//      be exposed on this interface in order to guarantee they
62: 	//      would be available. In the future, an external gRPC interface
63: 	//      likely will be required and the services which need registering
64: 	//      to the multiplexed listener will be greatly reduced. In the
65: 	//      very long term we want to get rid of this internal multiplexed
66: 	//      port/listener and instead have all component communications use
67: 	//      gRPC natively. For now though, if your service will need to
68: 	//      RECEIVE forwarded requests then it must be registered to this
69: 	//      interface.
70: 	//
71: 	// * In-Process - For routines running on the server we don't want them
72: 	//      to require network i/o as that will incur a lot of unnecessary
73: 	//      overhead. To avoid that we are utilizing the `grpchan` library
74: 	//      (github.com/fullstorydev/grpchan) and its `inprocgrpc` package.
75: 	//      The library provides the `inprocgrpc.Channel` which implements
76: 	//      both the `grpc.ServiceRegistrar` and `grpc.ClientConnInterface`
77: 	//      interfaces. Services get registered to the `Channel` and then
78: 	//      gRPC service clients can be created with the `Channel` used
79: 	//      for the backing `ClientConn`. When a client then uses the
80: 	//      `Invoke` or `NewStream` methods on the `Channel`, the `Channel`
81: 	//      will lookup in its registry of services to find the service's
82: 	//      server implementation and then have the standard
83: 	//      grpc.MethodDesc.Handler function handle the request. We use
84: 	//      a few variants of the in-process gRPC Channel. For now all
85: 	//      these channels are created and managed in server code but we
86: 	//      may need to move these into the higher level agent setup.
87: 	//
88: 	//      * Insecure + Unsafe - The insecure + unsafe gRPC Channel has
89: 	//           services registered to it that wont do typical ACL
90: 	//           resolution. Instead when the service resolves ACL tokens
91: 	//           a resolver is used which always grants unrestricted
92: 	//           privileges. Additionally, this "unsafe" variant DOES
93: 	//           NOT clone resources as they pass through the channel. Care
94: 	//           Must be taken to note mutate the data passed through the
95: 	//           Channel or else we could easily cause data race related
96: 	//           or consistency bugs.
97: 	//
98: 	//      * Insecure + Safe - Similar to the Insecure + Unsafe variant,
99: 	//           ACL resolution always provides an authorizer with unrestricted
100: 	//           privileges. However, this interface is concurrency/memory safe
101: 	//           in that protobuf messages passing through the interface are
102: 	//           cloned so that the client is free to mutate those messages
103: 	//           once the request is complete. All services registered to the
104: 	//           Unsafe variant should also be registered to this interface.
105: 	//
106: 	//      * Secure + Safe - This Channel will do typical ACL resolution from
107: 	//           tokens and will clone protobuf messages that pass through. This
108: 	//           interface will be useful for something like the HTTP server that
109: 	//           is crafting the gRPC requests from a user request and wants to
110: 	//           assume no implicit privileges by the nature of running on the
111: 	//           server. All services registered to the insecure variants should
112: 	//           also be registered to this interface. Additionally other services
113: 	//           that correspond to user requests should also be registered to this
114: 	//           interface.
115: 	//
116: 	//      Currently there is not a need for a Secure + Unsafe variant. We could
117: 	//      add it if needed in the future.
118: 
119: 	recoveryOpts := agentmiddleware.PanicHandlerMiddlewareOpts(s.loggers.Named(logging.GRPCAPI))
120: 
121: 	inprocLabels := []metrics.Label{{
122: 		Name:  "server_type",
123: 		Value: "in-process",
124: 	}}
125: 
126: 	statsHandler := agentmiddleware.NewStatsHandler(metrics.Default(), inprocLabels)
127: 
128: 	// TODO(inproc-grpc) - figure out what to do with rate limiting inproc grpc. If we
129: 	// want to rate limit in-process clients then we are going to need a unary interceptor
130: 	// to do that. Another idea would be to create rate limited clients which can be given
131: 	// to controllers or other internal code so that the whole Channel isn't limited but
132: 	// rather individual consumers of that channel.
133: 
134: 	// Build the Insecure + Unsafe gRPC Channel
135: 	s.insecureUnsafeGRPCChan = new(inprocgrpc.Channel).
136: 		// Bypass the in-process gRPCs cloning functionality by providing
137: 		// a Cloner implementation which doesn't actually clone the data.
138: 		// Note that this is only done for the Unsafe gRPC Channel and
139: 		// all the Safe variants will utilize the default cloning
140: 		// functionality.
141: 		WithCloner(inprocgrpc.CloneFunc(func(in any) (any, error) {
142: 			return in, nil
143: 		})).
144: 		WithServerUnaryInterceptor(middleware.ChainUnaryServer(
145: 			recovery.UnaryServerInterceptor(recoveryOpts...),
146: 			statsHandler.Intercept,
147: 		)).
148: 		WithServerStreamInterceptor(middleware.ChainStreamServer(
149: 			recovery.StreamServerInterceptor(recoveryOpts...),
150: 			agentmiddleware.NewActiveStreamCounter(metrics.Default(), inprocLabels).Intercept,
151: 		))
152: 
153: 	// Build the Insecure + Safe gRPC Channel
154: 	s.insecureSafeGRPCChan = new(inprocgrpc.Channel).
155: 		WithServerUnaryInterceptor(middleware.ChainUnaryServer(
156: 			recovery.UnaryServerInterceptor(recoveryOpts...),
157: 			statsHandler.Intercept,
158: 		)).
159: 		WithServerStreamInterceptor(middleware.ChainStreamServer(
160: 			recovery.StreamServerInterceptor(recoveryOpts...),
161: 			agentmiddleware.NewActiveStreamCounter(metrics.Default(), inprocLabels).Intercept,
162: 		))
163: 
164: 	// Build the Secure + Safe gRPC Channel
165: 	s.secureSafeGRPCChan = new(inprocgrpc.Channel).
166: 		WithServerUnaryInterceptor(middleware.ChainUnaryServer(
167: 			recovery.UnaryServerInterceptor(recoveryOpts...),
168: 			statsHandler.Intercept,
169: 		)).
170: 		WithServerStreamInterceptor(middleware.ChainStreamServer(
171: 			recovery.StreamServerInterceptor(recoveryOpts...),
172: 			agentmiddleware.NewActiveStreamCounter(metrics.Default(), inprocLabels).Intercept,
173: 		))
174: 
175: 	// create the internal multiplexed gRPC interface
176: 	s.internalGRPCHandler = agentgrpc.NewHandler(deps.Logger, config.RPCAddr, nil, s.incomingRPCLimiter)
177: 
178: 	return nil
179: }
